messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty PD-67890 triggered — p99 latency > 750ms in eu-west for model redwood-xl-8k-quant. SLO burn: 22% over last 5m. Autoscaler reported scale attempt failed. Link: https://pd.example.com/incidents/PD-67890 · runbook: https://confluence.redwood.infra/runbooks/latency-slo-burn
Tara: saw this on the dashboard — p99 jumped at 17:40 UTC, SSEs spiked too. Looks correlated with a recent canary deploy to the quantized variant.
Leo: acked PD-67890 (ack by Leo). I'm jumping in. Can someone confirm whether batcher queue depth is growing?
Maya: queue depth up on sidecar-batcher-3, avg inflight per worker 28 -> 90. Logs show `kv_cache_miss_rate` spiking.
Noah: customer-impact flag = partial_degradation. I see ~0.8% of requests >5s, ~0.02% 500s. Not widespread but affects streaming sessions -> visible to chat customers.
Tara: @Leo, @Sanjay, quick options: 1) rollback the canary, 2) force route eu-west traffic to xl-4k-fallback, 3) nudge autoscaler to +3 replicas, 4) clear KV cache warmups.
Sanjay: I'm happy to take rollback if we decide. But we should try routing first to avoid churn. If autoscaler didn't keep up, manual scale could help immediate headroom.
Leo: agree. Plan: (A) scale pool by +3 replicas, (B) enable fallback routing to xl-4k-fallback for non-enterprise customers, (C) monitor for 10m and then decide on rollback.
Maya: running `kubectl -n inference scale deployment inference-redwood-xl-8k-quant --replicas=6` now.
incident-bot: Action: `kubectl scale` initiated by Maya at 1778882512. Autoscaler override TTL 15m.
Noah: I applied routing rule to send 40% of eu-west traffic to xl-4k-fallback for routes with no hard pin. Config id: route-2026-03-15-01.
Tara: also triggered cache refresh on a handful of workers: `curl -X POST https://admin.eu-west.redwood/refresh_kv_cache -d '{"shard":"3"}'` — doing a rolling refresh to avoid stampeding.
Sanjay: watched the batcher metrics — inflight dropped from 90 -> 30 in ~90s after scaling and routing. p99 trending down to ~420ms (from 860ms).
Leo: good. Keep PD annotated: mitigation steps taken. PD note: scaled +3, routed 40% to fallback, cache refresh.
pagerduty-bot: PD-67890 status updated: acknowledged -> in_progress. Responders: Leo, Tara. Escalation halted.
Maya: small regression on a subset of gen routes that rely on model-specific tokenizer coldstart. I'm warming tokenizers on the new replicas with `preload_tokens=true` flag.
Noah: adding impact note for CS: "Some chat sessions experience delays >5s; users may see slower first responses in eu-west. No data leak or error rate increase beyond small 500 spike."
Tara: can we check whether recent quantization kernel selection changed? If the quantized path regressed, fallback routing is the right call.
Maya: confirmed: new kernel variant `qk_v2` was used by the canary and shows 20% higher decode latency on long sequences. Telemetry ID: tel-1778-qkv.
Leo: decision: keep fallback routing enabled; leave autoscaler override for 15m; no rollback yet. If p99 < 500ms for 10m, we close. If not, we'll rollback the canary.
Sanjay: I'll stay on this until 18:10 UTC then hand off to @Noah for the 00:00–08:00 coverage. Adding runbook notes: Runbook section 3.2 applied, commands and links logged to PD.
Tara: pinging infra to check if we should increase batcher concurrency limit as a follow-up (ticket INFRA-3249).
Noah: taking handoff at 18:10 UTC — will monitor dashboards and update PD. I've added a short checklist in PD: monitor p99, error rate, batcher depth, autoscaler events.
Leo: minor ask — capture a few traces for the slow requests (trace ids: trc-9812, trc-9813, trc-9817) and upload to S3: s3://redwood-diagnostics/pd/PD-67890/.
Maya: done, uploaded logs & heap profiles. Link: https://s3.console.aws.amazon.com/s3/object/redwood-diagnostics/pd/PD-67890/trace-bundle.tar.gz
incident-bot: PD-67890 annotated with mitigation steps and artifacts by Maya, Noah. Next check at 1778882833.
Tara: current status: p99 = 410ms, SLO burn decaying to 6% over 5m. Customer-impact still partial_degradation.
Noah: I'm monitoring; fallback routing remains in place. If everything looks green by 18:20 UTC we'll scale down the manual override and resume normal routing.
Leo: thumbs up. Thanks team. I'll write a short post-incident note and tag in postmortem if we need deeper investigation into qk_v2 kernel. :thumbsup:
Noah: taking ownership for the rotation handoff. Logged follow-up actions: INFRA-3249, MODEL-847 (kernel perf), CS-912 (customer comms).
Tara: closing loop: keep PD open until we remove overrides. If anyone sees a re-spike, ping here and re-escalate.
